location: England, Cheshire, Chester, Handbridge, Edgar Place
description:
A Roman quarry site south east of the Roman fort of Deva Victrix on the other side of the river Dee. A rock outcropping in the quarry has a carving of the goddess Minerva on the face of it, this is believed to have been carved while the quarry was in use, around the time the fort was being constructed. A small cave is cut into the rock behind the depiction of Minerva and this is believed to have been where votive offerings were placed.
The quarry went out of use some time in the early 2nd CE, and it is possible the shrine fell out of use at this time also if it was primarily used by labourers. But, the shrine has remained visible up until this day, and so may have continued to be used intermittently at any time between the present and its construction. The Historic England record for the quarry suggests it may have been adopted as a Christian shrine in later centuries to explain its survival, but there is no real evidence for this.
The stone structure surrounding the carving today was created in the 19th CE to protect it from damage.
